ops.title: Program path: STABLE wins; Staged() is strictly dominated
ops.body:
P4.0 (2026-07-31) resolved daemonkit's program-path question against evidence from the three
off-disk consumers (fusekit, cc-pool, cookiesync). Verdict: **STABLE** —
`~/.daemonkit/bin/<name>`, replaced by atomic rename. `Staged()` is deleted.

Why staged loses. TCC keys a bare Mach-O on its absolute path (`client_type = 1`); the designated
requirement is an anti-impersonation guard, not the lookup key, so a stable Developer ID does not
carry a grant across a path change. `~/.daemonkit/staged/<digest>/<name>` is a new absolute path per
build, outside any bundle — the plist Program churns every upgrade and the tree grows unswept.

The only *measured* TCC observation in the fleet confirms it: cookiesync's 0.16.0 migration
(cookiesync/CHANGELOG.md:118-135) — a path-churning bare Mach-O on a versioned Cellar path
re-prompted App Management + Automation on every `brew upgrade`, until the binary was nested in a
fixed-identity bundle.

Why staged has nothing left. Its one real advantage was surviving package-manager deletion of a
versioned install directory (a live fleet bug: a cask postflight kickstarts a Program `brew upgrade`
just deleted). A stable path under `~/.daemonkit/bin` lives outside any install directory too, so it
has that advantage as well — and does not churn. Strictly dominated.

Where the three grant-holders sit: fusekit runs a deploy-owned bundle under `~/Applications` and
hard-refuses relocation (fusekit/holder/plan.go:722-724) — a blocking consumer of any staged root,
not an abstention. cc-pool needs `InBundle`: staged would strip the App Group entitlement from its
self-exec children and break File Provider election
(cc-pool/scripts/assert-signed-topology.sh:135-151). cookiesync is already bundle-nested.

The verdict holds under BOTH candidate TCC key models, so [[tcc-key-model-for-bundle-nested-executables]]
does not gate it.

Consequence that must be handled wherever this lands: `Program.build()` digests the file at its own
path. Under staging each generation had its own path, so `build()` was stable per generation. Under a
stable path an upgrade rewrites the bytes under a *running* daemon, so `build()` returns the new
digest while the old daemon still serves the old bytes — every comparison of a running daemon's
published `Health.Build` against `Program.build()` mismatches for the whole replace-to-departure
window (`ensure.go:90`).

Related open backlog: 74be91d (helper agents bake versioned install paths into plists).
